title: Nested include! slice A, formatting only: rustfmt the 27 test fragments before they become modules
outcome: Slice A of w-05336c2d00a3 turns 27 `mod name { include!("f.rs"); }` blocks under src/tests into `#[path = "f.rs"] mod name;` declarations. `cargo fmt` does not reach an included file, and 22 of the 27 fragment files are not rustfmt-clean, so the wiring would fail `cargo fmt --all -- --check`. This candidate formats those files with rustfmt alone, and changes nothing else, so that the wiring candidate that follows is only wiring. The 27 blocks and fragments are listed in a note on this item.
acceptance: This item's contribution to the candidate commit changes only files under src/tests that slice A's wiring brings within `cargo fmt`'s reach: the fragment files of the listed blocks and the module files those fragments declare; every other path the commit changes belongs to another item, whose contribution is recorded with it.

For every path of this item's contribution, `git show PARENT:path | rustfmt --edition 2024` prints exactly the candidate's content of that path, where PARENT is the candidate's parent commit; the rustfmt version is recorded with the check.
The set of test names printed by `cargo test --bin termal -- --list` is the same on the candidate as on its parent, on one host.
No test reads or pins source text for this change.

completion.summary: 22 of the 27 test fragment files of slice A are now what `rustfmt --edition 2024` prints (the other 5 already were), with no hand edit and no wiring change, so the wiring that follows can pass cargo fmt. Landed on master in the batch commit fe5f485f; rustfmt equality was reproduced independently on Linux, test names are unchanged, both full gates passed on that exact commit and the evaluation passed all four criteria.
